blogs.title: 1.58 Bits Explained: What a Ternary LLM Means and Why It Matters
blogs.description: A friendly explainer for ML practitioners and students that breaks down what '1.58-bit' and ternary \/{-1,0,1\} weights mean in plain language. Covers the math intuition, how quantization maps continuous weights to {-1,0,1}, why adding zero improves modeling capacity over 1-bit, and a visual comparison to FP16, 8-bit and 4-bit models. Wraps with a short summary of the performance and efficiency trade-offs demonstrated by BitNet b1.58.

blogs.title: From FP16 to 1.58-bit: How BitNet b1.58 Cuts Latency, Memory and Energy
blogs.description: A deep-dive post for ML engineers that walks through the concrete runtime, memory and energy advantages reported for BitNet b1.58. Explains where the savings come from (replacing FP multiplies with integer additions, smaller weight transfers from DRAM, reduced KV cache), interprets the paper's scaling equivalences (e.g., 70B 1.58-bit ≈ 13B FP16 in cost), and suggests realistic expectations and limitations when adopting 1.58-bit models in production.

blogs.title: Training and Fine-tuning BitNet b1.58: A Practical Guide
blogs.description: A step-by-step, practitioner-focused guide covering how to train or fine-tune a ternary LLM: recommended hyperparameters, the absmean quantization routine, handling activations (8-bit scaling strategy), tips for initializing from FP16 checkpoints vs. training from scratch, and pitfalls to watch for. Includes suggested evaluation recipes (perplexity and downstream zero-shot tasks) and debugging tips when the quantized model diverges.

blogs.title: How to Run BitNet b1.58 Locally: Porting to Hugging Face, vLLM and llama.cpp
blogs.description: A how-to for developers and hobbyists that shows how to integrate BitNet b1.58 components into popular open-source tooling. Covers the LLaMA-alike components used (RMSNorm, SwiGLU, rotary embeddings), minimal code changes to swap Linear->BitLinear, recommended inference kernels (FasterTransformer + Ladder 2-bit kernel), and practical tips to test latency and memory on a GPU or CPU.

blogs.title: Designing Hardware for 1-bit LLMs: What Chip Architects Need to Know
blogs.description: A tech-enthusiast and hardware-audience post that explores the new computation paradigm enabled by ternary weights. Discusses architectural opportunities (systolic arrays optimized for integer addition, large on-chip SRAM for compressed weights, KV-cache compression), energy modeling comparisons, and concrete design directions for startups and researchers thinking about accelerators tailored to 1-bit / 1.58-bit LLMs.

blogs.title: Edge and Mobile LLMs: Making Large Models Fit on Small Devices with 1.58-bit Weights
blogs.description: A practical overview aimed at product builders and mobile engineers about bringing LLMs to edge devices using ternary compression. Covers memory & compute budgets on smartphones and edge CPUs, how 1.58-bit models enable longer contexts and lower latency on-device, trade-offs in accuracy, and a roadmap for a minimal working demo — from model conversion to benchmarking on common mobile hardware.

blogs.title: Long Contexts, Smaller Caches: How 1.58-bit Models Unlock Native Long-Sequence Support
blogs.description: Explains why KV caches are a major limiter for long-context LLMs and how reducing activations (from 16-bit to 8-bit, and compressible further) enables longer context windows without proportionally growing memory. The post walks through KV compression strategies, expected gains for doubling or quadrupling context length, and experiments you can run to validate latency and accuracy impacts.

blogs.title: Mixture-of-Experts Reimagined: The Case for 1-bit MoE LLMs
blogs.description: A conceptual post exploring how sparse MoE architectures could benefit from ternary weight compression: smaller memory footprint, fewer chips required for deployment, and lower network transfer overhead for activations. It outlines potential system designs, the remaining bottlenecks (routing, load balancing, and communication), and a research agenda for combining MoE with 1.58-bit training and inference.

blogs.title: The Real Cost of AI: Energy, Carbon and Dollars Saved by 1.58-bit LLMs
blogs.description: A data-driven writeup for decision-makers and sustainability-minded readers quantifying the environmental and economic impact of running ternary LLMs versus FP16. Uses the paper's energy-model claims to estimate electricity and CO2 savings across common deployment scenarios (cloud inference fleets, API endpoints, on-device usage), and provides an ROI-style checklist for teams considering migration to low-bit models.
